note: Anguilla, read in the Revised Statutes of Anguilla the Government publishes at laws.gov.ai (2022 Revision, 2026-10-31). Majority: the Age of Majority Act (R.S.A. c. A45, as at 15 December 2000), s. 2: a person attains full age at 18 instead of 21. Emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: the Employment of Children (Restriction) Act (R.S.A. c. E50, as at 15 December 2000) calls a child a person under 14 and bars employing one under 12 (save domestic work at home or light agricultural work on the parents' land), and any child before the close of school hours, before 6 a.m. or after 8 p.m., or more than two hours on a school day or a Sunday (s. 2(1)); so 12 is the youngest age a person may be employed, with those limits to 14 (not held). The Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act (c. E55, as at 15 December 2000) also bars a child under 14 from any industrial undertaking and any ship save a family one (ss. 3-4), and the Labour (Relations) Act (c. L7, as at 31 December 2022) sets no other minimum age that was found. Performers: no permit or exception lets a child under 12 be employed to perform; s. 2(4) of c. E50 only frees an unpaid performance in a charitable or educational entertainment from the hours limits, so paid performers under 12 are barred (my reading), and from 12 they work under the same limits as any child. Service: none of the 620 titles in the 2022 Revision (Acts and Regulations, read from its index) is a law of military or national service; Anguilla has a police force and no defence force, so service is none (a reading from the absence of any such law).
